comments.author: @cindyz53
comments.text: Just got back from visiting Greenland. An absolutely beautiful country. I enjoyed your video, especially seeing the places I have been. The communities are modern, and yet have retained much of the Inuit culture. It was interesting to see the Danish influence. While there has clearly been some negative aspects to their colonialism, Denmark also contributes a lot to the wellbeing of the country. While most Greenlanders hope to eventually be a self reliant country, they realize that it may take awhile before complete self sufficiency is achieved. I am hoping that the world will let them find their way economically and not exploit Greenland's resources. I also hope that tourism is managed in a way that does not overwhelm the country. I felt blessed to see it as it is now.

comments.author: @Globallifejourneyus
comments.text: Greenland makes you realize just how tough and adaptable people can be. The vast ice, brutal weather, and incredible isolation would feel overwhelming to me, yet people have built a life deeply connected to the land and sea. That contrast between the harsh environment and everyday life really stayed with me.

comments.text: What struck me most is the quiet dignity of the Inuit communities. When nature is that powerful and unforgiving, you quickly learn that individual ego means nothing—you survive by respecting the land and sticking close to your neighbors. Beautifully captured look into a world few of us will ever truly experience.
